risks.description: The verification result is immutable-commit-specific and does not automatically cover later repository changes.
risks.mitigation: Any later adoption change requires a separately reviewed commit-lock update and rerun.

risks.description: Offline verification depends on the three local repositories retaining the approved Git objects.
risks.mitigation: The verifier fails closed when a repository or approved commit is missing; approved commits also remain available through their repository histories.

risks.description: The original Manufacturing OS checkout contains pre-existing modified and untracked runtime or real-validation files.
risks.mitigation: Only approved committed objects and temporary detached clones were used. Before/after status was preserved, and the dirty-worktree test proves isolation.

risks.description: The local Node.js runtime differs from the frozen application baseline.
risks.mitigation: The verifier has no external dependencies, uses stable Node.js built-ins, and should be rerun under Node.js 24.18.0 when the pinned runtime is available.

risks.description: A passing deterministic verification could be mistaken for merge, production, architecture, or manufacturing approval.
risks.mitigation: The lock, reports, and verifier preserve checkpoint-review-required, keep P0-T02 not-started, and explicitly retain human authority.
